h: Torah and Reverence Keep the Heart Joined to Holiness

p: In this parsha there is written ten times
as is written in the Baal HaTurim.
is the name of the last attribute:
אֲנִי ה׳ שׁוֹכֵן בְּתוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
"I am Hashem, Who dwells amid Bnei Yisrael";
דְּהַיְינוּ יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ
is the union of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah;
Who is the Master of all powers.
And likewise in the Ten Commandments it opens
only that there is a kaf in the middle,
(רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא פִּנְחָס, חֵלֶק ג רנו, ב)
and in it is Ayin, etc."
That is, then it was explicit
That is, at that time Yisrael were
like one man with one heart,
and for this reason it is written there
ten times "I am Hashem your God,"
and likewise it indicates the union:
(מְלָכִים א יח, לט) ה׳ הוּא הָאֱלֹקִים
correspond to the first three sefiros.
And it opens: "You shall be holy,
for I, Hashem your God, am holy";
and this corresponds to the attribute of Chochmah,
that is, that the words of Torah be fixed,
which is the holiness of the Shabbos of Atika,
and it corresponds to Kesser Elyon
for meriting the holiness of Kesser Elyon
meriting the revelation of the light
which is the words of Torah,
which corresponds to the utterance "Let there be light";
and "light" five times in the passage
corresponds to the five books of the Torah
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ג, ה)
to be bound at the root
which is the intellect hidden from all thought
and this is as is written
(בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא, חֵלֶק ג פב, ב)
there is no cessation to the springing forth
And it says in the Raaya Mehemna
that in it the Cause of causes
for when one merits the holiness of Atika,
there is no cessation to the springing forth
and this is the meaning of "His light will rest upon it."
And it is similar to what is said:

p: it would be difficult why it is mentioned here.
It is understandable in the Ten Commandments,
the acceptance of the yoke of His Kingship;
where it speaks of the holiness of Yisrael:
And certainly one who worships idols
and what has he to do with holiness?
וּלְטַעַם זֶה דָּרְשׁוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קמט, א)
And for this reason they expounded in the Gemara (Shabbos 149a)
that even on a weekday it is forbidden to gaze at it;
that it is images of strange beasts
וְשֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁל מַעֲשִׂים וְכוּ׳
and of people in scenes, etc.;
That is, in the Gemara they said:
'Do not turn to' — to what is of your own mind."
Whereas according to the explanation of Tosafos,
images of beasts and the like,
only that it is a looking
by which one turns his heart to idle matters;
and this is what Rabbi Chanin said:
"Do not turn to what is of your own mind";
for one whose heart is full of the fear of Hashem
does not turn his heart to idle matters.
And Tosafos, who proved their view
מִמַּה דְּקָרוּ לְרַבִּי מְנַחֵם בֶּן סִימָאִי
from the fact that they called Rabbi Menachem ben Simai
because he did not gaze at the image on a coin,
which implies that others did gaze
as the image on a coin,
and they asked: "What piety is there, etc.?"
that although they needed the image on a coin
in order to know which coin it is,
and turning the heart is not relevant to it,
he would show it to others.
And in the holy Zohar too
it was difficult for it to explain the pasuk
וּמְפָרֵשׁ (חֵלֶק ג פג, סוֹף עַמּוּד ב)
and it explains (III 83b, at the end):
to gaze at the beauty of a woman,
And so Rabbi Shimon would, etc.,
and he would say to the companions:
And afterward the holy Zohar says:
'and you shall not make molten gods for yourselves.'"
And this follows what they said
"'There shall be no strange god in you' (Tehillim 81:10)
that is in a person's body?
he will come to impure thought
and bring the evil inclination into his heart,
"and you shall not make molten gods for yourselves";
only in a heart empty of Torah.
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
according to what the holy Zohar writes
and adultery and haughtiness of spirit."
At first the evil inclination comes lightly
and entices him to the joy of wine,
and through this it becomes with him
"At first He calls it a wayfarer,
and afterward He calls it a guest,
and afterward He calls it the master."
"Whoever sets his eye on his cup,
all forbidden unions seem to him like level ground."
And this is why there is called
the evil inclination for forbidden unions
for it begins with the joy of wine (mesech)
And here is said for the third time
and he will not turn to the idols.
And likewise according to the Gemara's explanation,
"Do not turn to what is of your own mind":
full of the fear of Hashem,
and he will not turn his heart to idle matters,
And if he turns his heart to idleness,
room will remain for the evil inclination,
for by meriting Chochmah and Binah,
from the joining of Chochmah and Binah,
which is the inwardness of Kesser Elyon;
and one merits the holiness of Atika,
which is bound at the root with Hashem Yisbarach:

inlineHeadings.text: Idle Attention Opens the Heart to Sin
Joining Wisdom and Reverence at the Root
